Inorganic Oxidant Demand

Source: R/chemdose_inorgdemand.R
chemdose_inorgdemand.Rd

Calculates Cl residual from inorganic scavengers present in the input water object: Mg, Fe, and Ammonia. The output water will have updated free_chlorine slot to reflect the chlorine residual after accounting for the inorganic demand. The mn, fe, and tot_nh3 slots will be set to 0, as they are assumed to be fully oxidized by the chlorine dose. Other products of the oxidation reactions will not be tracked or updated in the output water object. For a single water use chemdose_inorgdemand; to apply the model to a dataframe use chemdose_inorgdemand_df.

By default (use_chlorine_slot = FALSE), the output free_chlorine is cl2_dose minus the inorganic demand, and any free chlorine already in the water is overwritten (with a warning). Set use_chlorine_slot = TRUE to add the existing free_chlorine slot to cl2_dose before the demand is subtracted. If cl2_dose is not specified, the existing free_chlorine slot is used (with a warning when use_chlorine_slot = FALSE). The function errors if the inorganic demand is greater than the available chlorine.

The inorganic demand of ammonia is calculated assuming all ammonia is converted to nitrogen gas, not considering the conversion of ammonia to nitrate. For chloramine chemistry, use chemdose_chloramine if interested in more precise breakpoint chlorination calculations.

Usage

chemdose_inorgdemand(water, cl2_dose, use_chlorine_slot = FALSE)

chemdose_inorgdemand_df(
  df,
  input_water = "defined",
  output_water = "oxidized",
  pluck_cols = FALSE,
  water_prefix = TRUE,
  keep_dose_cols = FALSE,
  cl2_dose = "use_col",
  use_chlorine_slot = "use_col"
)

Arguments

water

Input water object with mn, fe, and tot_nh3 slots defined. The free_chlorine slot must also be defined when the slot is used (use_chlorine_slot = TRUE or cl2_dose not specified).

cl2_dose

Chlorine dose in mg/L Cl2.

use_chlorine_slot

Defaults to FALSE. When TRUE, the existing free_chlorine slot in the water is added to cl2_dose. If cl2_dose is not specified, only the chlorine slot will be used, regardless of use_chlorine_slot.

df

a data frame containing a water class column, which has already been computed using define_water_df. The df may include columns for the chlorine dose (cl2_dose) and use_chlorine_slot.

input_water

name of the column of water class data to be used as the input for this function. Default is "defined".

output_water

name of the output column storing updated water class object. Default is "oxidized".

pluck_cols

Extract the free_chlorine slot into a new numeric column for easy access. Default to FALSE.

water_prefix

Append the output_water name to the start of the plucked columns. Default is TRUE.

keep_dose_cols

Option to keep the original chemical dose columns in the output data frame. Default is FALSE.

Value

chemdose_inorgdemand returns a water class object with updated free_chlorine slot that reflects the chlorine residual.

chemdose_inorgdemand_df returns a data frame containing a water class column with updated free_chlorine, mn, fe, and tot_nh3 slots. Optionally, it also adds a column for free_chlorine.

Examples


water1<-define_water(ph = 7, alk = 70, mn = 1, fe = 2, tot_nh3 = 1)
#> Warning: Major ions, TDS, and conductivity are all missing; assuming ideal conditions.
#> Ionic strength will be "NA" and activity coefficients will be 1.
cl_residual <- chemdose_inorgdemand(water1, 20)

# Use the existing free chlorine in the water
water2 <- define_water(ph = 7, alk = 70, mn = 1, fe = 2, tot_nh3 = 1, free_chlorine = 12)
#> Warning: Major ions, TDS, and conductivity are all missing; assuming ideal conditions.
#> Ionic strength will be "NA" and activity coefficients will be 1.
cl_residual <- chemdose_inorgdemand(water2, use_chlorine_slot = TRUE)

# \donttest{
example_df <- water_df %>%
  dplyr::mutate(mn = 20, fe = 0.5, tot_nh3 = 0.2) %>%
  define_water_df() %>%
  chemdose_inorgdemand_df(cl2_dose = 5, pluck_cols = TRUE)
#> Warning: Existing free_chlorine slot will be overridden based on recent dose. To sum
#> results instead, set `use_chlorine_slot = TRUE`. (6 rows affected.)

example_df <- water_df %>%
  dplyr::mutate(mn = 20, fe = 0.5, tot_nh3 = 0.2) %>%
  define_water_df() %>%
  dplyr::mutate(ClDose = seq(3, 14, 1)) %>%
  chemdose_inorgdemand_df(cl2_dose = ClDose, output_water = "chlorinated")
#> Warning: Existing free_chlorine slot will be overridden based on recent dose. To sum
#> results instead, set `use_chlorine_slot = TRUE`. (6 rows affected.)

# Use the free_chlorine already in each water instead of a dose
example_df <- water_df %>%
  dplyr::mutate(mn = 20, fe = 0.5, tot_nh3 = 0.2, free_chlorine = 4) %>%
  define_water_df() %>%
  chemdose_inorgdemand_df(use_chlorine_slot = TRUE, pluck_cols = TRUE)
# }
